title: Why inherent justice cannot justify at the severe bar
source_text: XXVIII. Quo vero Theologi nostri negant nos justificari, sive justos esse coram Deo per justitiam propriam, & nobis inhaerentem, verum per solam Christi justitiam nobis imputatam, mens eorum est, neminem tam justum & sanctum reperiri, quin apud Dei tribunal mortis & damnationis reus comperiatur, si Deus nolit cum ipso misericorditer agere, sed juxta legis rigorem illum districte judicare. Quoniam videlicet omnes per legem divinam peccati convincuntur, neque maledictionem quam lex peccatoribus omnibus denuntiat, ullo modo vitare & effugere possunt virtute & merito propriae justitiae, & bonorum quae fecerint operum, si Deus nullam ipsis gratiam facere velit, sed jure suo erga eos uti. Quod vero fideles liberantur a morte & perditione aeterna, quam peccatis suis juste commeruerunt, & in Dei filios & regni coelestis haeredes adoptantur, id unice deberi merito mortis & passionis Christi, quam Deus ita nobis donat & communicat, ut vere nostra sit & censeri debeat, non autem ulla ex parte bonis quibusdam nostris operibus, aut alicui justitiae nostrae, cujus merito atque dignitate Deus moveatur atque impellatur, ut nos ab exitio nobis alioqui debito liberet, & jus ad vitae aeternae haereditatem concedat.
pass_a_gloss: But when our theologians deny that we are justified or are just before God by our own inherent righteousness, and affirm it only by Christ’s righteousness imputed to us, their meaning is that no one is found so just and holy that he would not be discovered liable to death and damnation at God’s tribunal if God were unwilling to deal mercifully with him and judged him strictly according to the law’s rigor. For all are convicted of sin by the divine law, and by the virtue and merit of their own righteousness and of the good works they have done they can in no way avoid and escape the curse which the law denounces to all sinners, if God wills to show them no grace but to use his right toward them. But that the faithful are freed from the eternal death and perdition they justly deserved by their sins, and are adopted as God’s children and heirs of the heavenly kingdom, is owed solely to the merit of Christ’s death and passion, which God so gives and communicates to us that it is truly ours and ought to be so reckoned—not in any part to certain good works of ours or to any righteousness of ours by whose merit and dignity God would be moved and driven to free us from the ruin otherwise due to us and to grant a right to the inheritance of eternal life.
pass_b_english: Denial of inherent formal justification means: none stand law’s rigor without mercy.
Freedom and adoption are owed solely to Christ’s communicated passion-merit, not our works’ dignity.

lemmas.gloss: merit of Christ’s death and passion
